overview.body: This is a BUILD unit: Module 3 begins! Your game gets a main menu, and for the first time it remembers you. Save in the middle of a trip, close the program, and load it later to pick up right where you left off.

mentorQuote.quote: Every game you've played that lets you quit and come back later is doing what you'll build this week: write the game down, read it back. It's the first time your program outlives a single run, and that changes what you can build.

objectives: Wrap your game in a main menu loop: New Game, Load Saved Game, Quit
Replace the yes or no question with an OPTIONS menu
Write your game to a file with open(), write(), and close()
Use try/except FileNotFoundError so a missing file can't crash your game
overview.keyConceptsText:
Chapter 6: writing and reading files, converting numbers to and from strings, and exceptions (try/except)
Chapter 5: returning more than one value, and returning None
overview.textbookReference: Starting Out with Python, 6th Edition by Tony Gaddis, Chapter 6, plus Chapter 5's value-returning functions. .rstrip() is from Chapter 8; this lab uses it to remove the newline from each line it reads, as Chapter 6 does.

content.body: A clean starting point. Your finished Lab 2.3 game becomes Lab 3.1, and you check that it still plays exactly as it did before you add anything new.

Lab 2.3 is a complete, working game, and this lab wraps it rather than rewriting it: a main menu around the outside, and a way to save and load a game in progress. Every checkpoint after this one assumes your game keeps going from Houston and San Antonio, because that's where a game gets saved. Your library carries forward unchanged.

content.body: A main menu, the first thing a player sees: start a new game, load a saved one, or quit. After a session ends, the menu comes back.

The menu is one more loop, while in_program:, around everything after the banner. Choose 3 and the loop's flag turns False; continue jumps back to the top, where the loop sees the flag and stops. New Game asks for a name and starts the session totals. Load can't load anything yet, so for now it says there's no save file and starts a new game, which is exactly what it will do in CP5 when there isn't one. Load is checked before New Game, so that fallback can run New Game next.

content.quote: Count the loops: in_program, play_again, playing, and the travel loop. Four, and each has one job. The menu picks what to do. play_again runs one game after another. playing runs one leg after another. The travel loop runs one turn after another. If you're not sure where a line goes, ask which of those jobs it's part of.

content.body: A three-way choice in place of Keep going this trip? (y/n): . Each time you arrive in Houston or San Antonio, you can continue the journey, save and quit, or quit without saving. Save and quit comes alive in CP4; this checkpoint wires up the other two.

A yes or no question can't hold three answers, so it becomes a menu, validated by get_valid_int() like every other menu. Quitting without saving still ends the game with a report, and the report should say why it ended. A Boolean flag, quit_without_saving, carries that from inside the loop to the status line after it. Every game starts it at False, so it can't leak from one game into the next.

content.quote: Players hate guessing what a menu choice did. When I quit a trip, the report should say I quit, not Trip Incomplete like something went wrong. One flag set where it happens, one line in the status check. That's the whole fix.

content.code:
def save_game(player_name, current_city, total_miles, total_turns,
              total_hazards, total_escaped, games_played,
              session_miles, session_hazards):
    """
    Save the game to SAVE_FILE, one value on each line.

    Args:
        player_name (str): The player's name
        current_city (str): Where the player is now
        total_miles (int): Miles so far this game
        total_turns (int): Turns so far this game
        total_hazards (int): Hazards faced so far this game
        total_escaped (int): Hazards escaped so far this game
        games_played (int): Games finished this session
        session_miles (int): Miles in the finished games
        session_hazards (int): Hazards in the finished games
    """
    outfile = open(SAVE_FILE, 'w')
    outfile.write(player_name + '\n')
    outfile.write(current_city + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(total_miles) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(total_turns) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(total_hazards) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(total_escaped) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(games_played) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(session_miles) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(session_hazards) + '\n')
    outfile.close()
    print('Game saved!')

content.body: Load, for real. Choose 2 at the main menu and the game reads savegame.txt, welcomes you back, and picks up right where you saved. No file? You get a new game, as before.

readline() reads one line, and it keeps the '\n' at the end, so .rstrip('\n') takes it off. Every line comes back as a string, so the numbers go through int(). If the file isn't there, open() raises FileNotFoundError; try/except catches it and the function returns None, Python's value for "nothing". Otherwise it returns all nine values at once, and the caller unpacks them into its own variables, in the same order. One more flag, resumed_game, tells the next game to keep the loaded values instead of starting over.

content.code:
def load_game():
    """
    Load the game from SAVE_FILE.

    Returns:
        tuple: The nine saved values, in the order save_game() writes
        them, or None if there is no save file
    """
    try:
        infile = open(SAVE_FILE, 'r')
        player_name = infile.readline().rstrip('\n')
        current_city = infile.readline().rstrip('\n')
        total_miles = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        total_turns = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        total_hazards = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        total_escaped = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        games_played = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        session_miles = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        session_hazards = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        infile.close()
        return (player_name, current_city, total_miles, total_turns,
                total_hazards, total_escaped, games_played,
                session_miles, session_hazards)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
